description: For a MARRIED borrower on an income-driven federal student loan plan, prices the filing-status decision: filing separately removes the spouse's income from the payment calculation, which lowers the monthly payment and often the lifetime cost by tens of thousands of dollars. Returns both sides with the monthly and lifetime difference. IMPORTANT: this models the LOAN side only. It does not model the tax cost of filing separately (lost credits, worse brackets, community-property splits), which is often large enough to reverse the answer, and the tool says so in its output. Use it whenever a married borrower asks about IDR, RAP, PSLF or how to file.

balance.description: Current federal loan balance in dollars.

borrowerAgi.description: The borrower's own annual adjusted gross income in dollars.

dependents.description: Number of qualifying dependents. A spouse is NOT a dependent.

loanType.description: Federal loan type. Drives plan eligibility, not just the rate.

ratePct.description: Weighted average interest rate as a percentage, e.g. 6.54 for 6.54%.

spouseAgi.description: The spouse's annual AGI in dollars. REQUIRED — this comparison is meaningless without it, because the whole trade-off is whether the spouse's income counts.

name: compare_married_filing_jointly_vs_separately_student_loans
title: Compare filing jointly vs separately for student loans
